title: Tactical prefill exploration — sprint brain dump (Jun 11 2029)
body:
Context
Quick brain dump after the Tuesday deep-dive. We're in sprint-67 window but pulled a 2-day microcycle to validate a handful of prefill hypotheses that keep showing up in oncall. This is intentionally rough — notes-to-self + things for the next async sync.

Attendees
- Aisha (owner)
- Miguel (kernel lead)
- Priya (kv cache + metrics)
- Ben (batching heuristics)
- Zoe (oncall / incident owner)

Topline summary (1–2 lines)
Prefill shadowing shows a repeatable microburst pattern where short-form requests cause KV cache churn and a downstream batch-splitting event that spikes p99 for ~120–240ms during transitions. Small kernel scheduling tweaks help, but the larger win looks to be a lightweight prefetch anchor plus a softer batch coalescer.

Why this matters now
- Customer apps (chat + assistant) are sensitive to small p99 regressions; we saw 6 regressions in the last week tied to cache eviction storms.
- Dedicated customers have tighter SLOs; a mitigation we can push quickly (config toggle) would reduce incidents.

Observations/Data points
- Repro: traffic generator replay of 10k mixed chat sessions (~80% short messages, 20% long) shows a consistent spike at the moment cohorts transition (every ~3.5s).
- Metric snapshot (A -> B -> C transition window): p50 stayed ~34ms, p95 ~78ms, p99 bumped 230–320ms for the 200–600ms window after cohort switch.
- KV cache eviction rate increased by 18% during bursts (trace id run: rrun-20290610-01).
- The kernel scheduling trace shows 2 back-to-back small kernels taking 1.5x expected time when prefetch slots are contested.

Hypotheses (ranked)
1) Anchor-prefetch hypothesis: If we issue a small, low-cost anchor prefill for the most-likely KV keys when a short-form request arrives, we prevent eviction churn during the next 150ms window.
2) Soft-coalesce hypothesis: Make batch coalescer slightly more tolerant to small inter-arrival jitter (increase window by +8ms for 'hot' cohorts) to avoid unnecessary split.
3) Eviction prioritization hypothesis: Mark prefill-originated KV items with soft pin so eviction prefers older cold cohorts for 200ms.
4) Kernel-run smoothing: Add micro-yield between tiny kernels to reduce lock contention on the prefetch queue.

Experiments we ran (notes + results)
- EXP-4821 (anchor-prefill, 20% traffic)
  - Implementation: lightweight prefetch triggered for top-3 KV keys derived from local model-prefetch heuristics. Prefetch runs at low priority and writes to shadow-cache (not primary) for A/B.
  - Result: p99 down by ~45ms in affected cohort, cache eviction rate reduced 11%. CPU + memory delta negligible.
  - Caveat: For very long-running sessions, shadow writes sometimes led to duplicated recompute in next token — fixable but needs attention.

- EXP-4822 (soft-coalesce param +8ms, whole cluster toggle)
  - Result: reduced batch-splits by 9%, p99 improved ~28ms, but average batch latency rose ~3ms. Customer-visible impact minimal.

- EXP-4823 (eviction pin TTL=200ms)
  - Result: marginal improvement in churn; eviction counters dropped 6% but memory pressure sometimes increased on hotspots. Risk: may cause longer tail for cold-starts.

Engineering notes / implementation quirks
- Kernel-level memguard: Miguel notes that micro-yielding introduces a spin-sleep pattern on a hot path; prefer a nanosleep-based backoff rather than thread-yield.
- Prefill tagging: we need a compact tag in the KV item metadata to indicate 'prefill:shadow' that won't bloat storage. Use a 1-byte flag in the on-disk tag.
- Batch coalescer: Ben found a race where coalescer window update and batch-split decision can interleave. Added a small compare-and-swap in the coalescer controller; need review.

Actionable next steps (owners and rough ETA)
- Merge EXP-4821 as 'shadow-prefill' behind toggle + telemetry (Aisha) — ETA: 2029-06-14.
- Add nanosleep backoff in kernel prefetch queue (Miguel) — ETA: 2029-06-16; must land before enabling live for large clusters.
- Coalescer CAS fix + unit tests (Ben) — ETA: 2029-06-15.
- Run 48h soak on a dedicated fleet with toggle ramp (Priya + Zoe) — start 2029-06-17.
- Update runbook snippet for oncall with new toggle and rollback steps (Zoe) — ETA: 2029-06-13.

Open questions / things to decide
- TTL semantics for shadow-prefill: do we expose to customers or keep internal? (ops prefers internal to avoid surprising billing).
- Metric gating: what p99 delta warrants automatic rollout? Suggested threshold: >= 20ms improvement sustained over 6h.
- Memory clamp: if we pin prefill items, do we also clamp per-shard memory window? Risk of hotspotting.

Notes-to-self and scribbles
- If shadow-prefill duplicates compute, we may try a prefetch soft-hint that only populates kv indexes, delaying full value until first read. Might be cleaner.
- Add a debug flag that prints cohort-id + prefill-tag in logs for five minutes after deploy: helps correlate in traces.
- Revisit the 'increase window by +8ms' number — it came from sampling; run microbench to find knee point.

Meeting artifacts / references
- Experiment PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821
- Jira epic: JIRA-RT-9821 (prefill microburst mitigation)
- Proposal draft on Confluence: CONFLUENCE-RT-2394

Decision log (if we merge)
- We agreed to ship shadow-prefill behind a toggle and run a staggered rollout with guardrails (max 20% traffic -> 50% -> 100%) and a rollback hook at each step.

Quick checklist before enabling cluster-wide
- [ ] Merge PR + telemetry (histogram for prefill-hit, eviction-by-tag)
- [ ] Kernel backoff landed + tested
- [ ] Coalescer CAS + tests in main
- [ ] Soak started on dedicated fleet
- [ ] Oncall runbook updated

Appendix: quick commands and trace ids
- local-replay: tools/traffic_replay --profile shortburst --seed 20290610 --scale 10k
- trace ids: rrun-20290610-01 (primary), rrun-20290611-02 (exp run)
- PRs to watch: #4821, #4822, #4823

End of dump — will tidy for the sprint review.
